parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Two capacitors X and Y are connected in series to a power supply of voltage $V$, as shown in Fig. 6.1.

{{figure:figure_6_1}}

The capacitance of X is $C_X$ and the capacitance of Y is $C_Y$.

Derive an expression, in terms of $C_X$ and $C_Y$, for the combined capacitance $C_T$ of the capacitors in this circuit.
Explain your reasoning.

parts.label: (b)
parts.part_stem: Two capacitors P and Q are connected in parallel to a power supply of voltage $V$. The capacitance of P is $200 \mu\text{F}$. The capacitance $C_Q$ of Q can be varied between $0$ and $400 \mu\text{F}$. When $C_Q = 0$, the total energy stored in the capacitors is $2.5 \text{mJ}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Show that the supply voltage $V$ is $5.0 \text{V}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the total energy, in $\text{mJ}$, stored in the capacitors when $C_Q$ has its maximum value.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
On Fig. 6.2, sketch the variation of the total energy $E$ stored in the capacitors with $C_Q$, as $C_Q$ varies from $0$ to $400 \mu\text{F}$.

{{figure:figure_6_2}}
